chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: 'Ubays ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Jabla, from Miskeen al-Rahhal, from Ali ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Umayra bint Nufayl, who said: I heard al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) saying:

The matter that you are expecting will not occur until a time comes that you disavow each other, spit at the face of each other, and one of you declares unbelief against the other, and you curse each other. I said to him: 'There will be no goodness in that time!' He said: 'All the goodness will be in that time. Our Qa'im will rise and do away with all of that.'

key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: The Matter (referring to the rise of the Qa'im)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the time before the Qa'im rises according to Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Husayn (AS) identifies the era of the Great Occasion (al-Ghayba al-Kubra) as a time of intense fragmentation where mutual disavowal (*al-barā' min ba'd*) and accusations of disbelief (*al-takfīr*) become prevalent among the Shia. This highlights the scholarly concept of *al-barā'* not merely as theological separation, but as a social reality of purging the community from false adherents during the final tests before the Qa'im's rise. Despite the chaos, the Imam affirms that the ultimate good lies in the imminent appearance of the Imam who will rectify these divisions.
